title: A Kitchen for the Summer Again
premise: Wendell Halloran, a cellist whose hands failed him during one catastrophic final performance, retreats to the small town of Marrow Creek to restore an inherited orchard house and keep his heart as silent as his cello. When he discovers the orchard deed inexplicably lists two names—his own and that of Theo Vance, the man he loved and abandoned ten years ago—he is forced into a summer of shared labor, reluctant honesty, and the slow thaw of found family among the orchard's ragtag caretakers. As Wendell rehearses the confession he has carried for a decade, Theo's health begins to fail, compressing years of silence into one dwindling season. In the end, Wendell speaks the sentence at last—not to reclaim what was lost, but to offer what remains—and chooses to stay in Marrow Creek, playing again not for stages but for the people who became his home.
about_author: Dominic Nystrom is a former orchard hand from the Pacific Northwest who writes quiet romances about second chances and stubborn land. He lives with his partner and an ill-tempered peach tree he refuses to give up on.

chapters.title: The Last Note That Broke
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. A flashback-tinged opening: the night his hands seized mid-concert, the walk offstage, the decade since. Present-day Wendell arrives in Marrow Creek to claim a house he barely remembers inheriting. Emotional beat: numbness mistaken for peace.

chapters.title: A Deed With Two Names
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. At the county office, Wendell discovers the orchard deed bears both his name and Theo Vance's—his first love, gone ten years without a word. The clerk shrugs; the paper doesn't lie. Emotional beat: dread blooming where grief had calcified.

chapters.title: The Man Under the Peach Trees
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo, tending the orchard alone, learns a stranger has arrived claiming half his land—then recognizes Wendell and says nothing. Emotional beat: fury and longing colliding behind a polite mask.

chapters.title: Terms of Coexistence
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The two strike a brittle bargain: split the summer, split the harvest, never discuss the past. Wendell moves into the drafty east room. Emotional beat: armed truce, charged proximity.

chapters.title: The Orchard Keepers
chapters.summary: Ensemble chapter, rotating close-third among neighbors: Priya the jam-maker, old Sam the pruner, teenager Junie who bikes in daily. They adopt Wendell before he consents to it. Emotional beat: warmth arriving uninvited.

chapters.title: Blisters and Borrowed Tools
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Manual work wrecks his already damaged hands; Theo silently leaves salve outside his door. First real conversation in ten years, all subtext. Emotional beat: tenderness disguised as logistics.

chapters.title: Junie Asks the Wrong Question
chapters.summary: Junie's POV. The teen bluntly asks why two grown men hate each other over fruit trees. Neither answers well, and Junie starts her own investigation through town records. Emotional beat: comic pressure on buried wounds.

chapters.title: What the Cello Remembers
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo finds Wendell's abandoned cello case in the barn and understands, finally, the scale of what was lost that night onstage. He almost apologizes for something he can't name. Emotional beat: pity curdling into ache.

chapters.title: Storm Damage
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. A summer storm flattens a row of trees; the whole town turns out to save the orchard. Working shoulder to shoulder, Wendell and Theo nearly touch the truth. Emotional beat: crisis as intimacy.

chapters.title: The Letter He Never Sent
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Priya finds a ten-year-old unsent letter in the house's walls—Wendell's own apology, written the week he left. Theo reads it alone. Emotional beat: exposure without consent.

chapters.title: Cold Storage
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Wounded by the letter's excuses, Theo goes glacial; Wendell, humiliated, considers leaving. Junie hides his bus ticket. Emotional beat: rock bottom of the estrangement.

chapters.title: The Doctor's Waiting Room
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. She drives Theo to a cardiology appointment in the city and learns his diagnosis is worse than he admits. She swears secrecy, then regrets it. Emotional beat: loyalty beginning its war with truth.

chapters.title: First Harvest
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The first ripe peaches come in; the town celebrates. Theo, pale and laughing, lets himself be happy for one evening, and Wendell falls all the way back in love. Emotional beat: joy shadowed by ticking clock.

chapters.title: Loyalty's Ledger
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya wrestles with her promise while watching Wendell rehearse his confession nightly to an empty kitchen. Sam counsels her: some truths belong to their owners. Emotional beat: the theme made explicit.

chapters.title: The Sentence, Rehearsed
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell finally drafts the sentence aloud—I left because I was afraid you'd see me fail—and loses his nerve when Theo appears in the doorway. Emotional beat: courage failing at the threshold.

chapters.title: Collapse Among the Rows
chapters.summary: Junie's POV. Theo collapses during picking; Junie witnesses it and, bound by no promises, tells Wendell everything. Emotional beat: the secret detonating.

chapters.title: Confrontation in the Cold Room
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell confronts Theo, who admits he sought him out via the deed deliberately—wanting to die near him but unable to ask. Anger breaks open into the decade-old truth on both sides. Emotional beat: climax of confession.

chapters.title: Surgery Season
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Hospital chapters compressed: the operation, the waiting room full of orchard keepers, Wendell playing soft cello in the corridor against every rule. Emotional beat: fear transfigured into devotion.

chapters.title: What Belonging Costs
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Theo recovers slowly and offers Wendell a clean exit—the deed signed over, no obligations. Wendell refuses and instead proposes they rebuild the orchard together, on purpose this time. Emotional beat: choosing to stay.

chapters.title: The Kitchen for the Summer Again
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. The title scene: the restored farmhouse kitchen filled with preserving day—Priya's jam, Junie's chaos, Sam's stories, two men cooking side by side like they always meant to. Emotional beat: found family made literal.

chapters.title: An Audience of Neighbors
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. At the harvest festival, Wendell performs publicly for the first time since the catastrophe—shaking hands, imperfect sound, Theo in the front row. He plays the whole piece. Emotional beat: redemption without erasure.

chapters.title: Present Tense
chapters.summary: Alternating Wendell/Theo POV. Autumn arrives; the deed is amended to both names permanently. On the porch, Wendell says the last unrehearsed sentence—I'm staying—and Theo answers in kind. Emotional beat: love moved out of the past tense, at last.
